answer: An agent economy can anchor trust in a small set of verified anchor identities and require every new vertex in the trust graph to earn endorsements from existing anchors before it can transact. Think of reputation spreading like seeds across a meadow: one isolated fake account cannot mint credibility on its own, because endorsements only flow from anchors with a long, costly history. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of separate endorsement relationships, each requiring real work or a refundable bond, so a Sybil swarm stays cheap to spot and expensive to grow.
